analysis: Examined all units. ProviderLoop+AutoUpdate.swift and AutoUpdateController.swift changes are log/doc wording only (quarantine message no longer says 'after failed starts'). The auto-update flow (lease claim, stage, drain, commit, App Attest worker stop, restart ownership checks) is unchanged and was reviewed for context: commit and restart paths re-check cancellation and drain ownership (ProviderLoop+AutoUpdate.swift:290, 318, 342), and the App Attest worker must exit before commit or restart (lines 124, 131), consistent with TB-011/T-053 expectations. SelfUpdater.swift only widens `now` from private to internal (module-visible), which is a harmless clock seam for the extension; no new external exposure. The new SelfUpdater+Rollback.swift adds an operator rollback planner/executor. It takes a cross-process update lease (beginUpdateSession, timeout 0), runs session.recover, and requires the installed release to match the recorded one (liveMatches) and the predecessor to verify (verifyPredecessor) before rollback. It re-plans under the lease and compares from/to/generation to the confirmed plan (lines 114-117) to guard against TOCTOU. It delegates to the existing journaled UpdateSession.rollback, with failure recovery under the held lease. The monotonic check isNewer(installed, predecessor) prevents rolling forward. Rollback to a retained, verified predecessor is operator-initiated and local (same-UID operator, who already can replace the binary per T-013/T-043). I identified no regression. Remaining questions not visible in this batch: UpdateSession.rollback, verifyPredecessor and liveMatches implementations (signature and CodeDirectory verification of the predecessor, quarantine semantics), the CLI caller of rollBackToPredecessor, and whether rollback to an older build interacts with App Attest qualification revocation (T-054) and coordinator minimum-version policy. These are outside the supplied evidence and warrant integration-level checking.
